body:
### Problem

Most work in a GitHub-hosted repo starts life as a GitHub issue, but vincent knows nothing about GitHub. Creating a task for an existing issue means opening the issue in a browser, copying the title into the new-task form, copying the body into the description, and then re-typing anything the workflow needs as a declared field. The issue number and URL survive only if the human remembers to paste them, and the agent that eventually runs the workflow never sees the issue's labels, author or link at all — a workflow prompt cannot say "fix the bug described below" because there is nothing in the §8.4 template context to interpolate.

Today there is no GitHub concept anywhere in the tree: `store.Project` has no remote or host field, `config.yaml` has no `github` key, and `workflow.RenderContext` has no issue surface.

### Proposed solution

When a project is GitHub-based **and** GitHub integration is enabled, let the human pick a GitHub issue while creating a task. The pick prefills the task and is carried into the workflow's template context so issue details are available to prompts and commands.

This is the first piece of a broader GitHub integration; **checking on pull requests is the intended next piece** and should not be designed out, but it is explicitly not in scope here.

**Detection and enablement.** "GitHub-based" is derived, not stored: parse the project's `origin` remote for a github.com host at the point of use. No new `Project` column and no migration. "Enabled" is a `config.yaml` toggle, so a user who does not want the daemon reading GitHub can turn it off; hot reload applies as it does for the rest of config.

**Authentication.** Prefer the `gh` CLI (`gh issue list/view --json …`) and fall back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` from the daemon's inherited environment when `gh` is absent or unauthenticated. vincent stores no credential of its own, which keeps spec §2's "secret management" non-goal intact and matches how the daemon already drives external CLIs. The daemon makes the call — clients never talk to GitHub, per the ownership invariant. `gitx.RemoteTimeout` is the precedent for bounding it.

**Surfaces.**

- TUI: an issue row in the new-task form, opening a picker in the same shape as the existing project/workflow/agent pickers (`internal/tui/newtaskpicker.go`). Default listing is open issues, newest first, narrowable by typed text; the row belongs in the §15 form order, before title.
- API: a `github_issue` field on `POST /v1/tasks`, plus whatever read endpoint the picker needs to list issues for a project. The TUI holds no state the daemon doesn't have, so this exists regardless of the TUI.
- CLI: `vincent task create --github-issue 123`, resolved daemon-side, with explicit flags winning over anything the issue would have prefilled; and a list command (`vincent github issues`) so issues can be browsed without opening the TUI.

**What the pick fills in.** Title from the issue title, description from the issue body, a link line carrying the issue number and URL appended to the description so a task read on its own still points back, and a best-effort mapping of issue metadata (labels, assignee, milestone) onto the workflow's declared `fields:` (§8.1.2) where the names line up. Everything lands in the form's editable rows — nothing is locked, and a human can rewrite or clear any of it before creating. Because the mapping guesses, it must be visible in the form before creation rather than applied silently at run time.

**Template context.** A new top-level `.Issue` in `workflow.RenderContext` (number, title, body, URL, state, labels, author, …), zero-valued when no issue is linked so a template shared between linked and unlinked tasks can test it — the same convention `.Loop`'s `Index: 0` already uses. Rendering must stay a pure, offline operation.

**Freshness.** The issue is fetched once at task creation and persisted on the task; every step renders from that snapshot. This is the same reasoning that makes vincent snapshot the workflow YAML at creation: a run is reproducible, no network call enters the step path, and a step render still cannot fail for an external reason. An issue edited on GitHub after task creation is deliberately not reflected.

**When GitHub is unavailable** — `gh` missing, not authenticated, no token, rate-limited, offline — the issue row is not offered and the daemon logs the concrete reason. In addition, `vincent doctor` gains a row reporting `gh` presence and authentication state, so the diagnosis lives beside the other environment checks rather than only in the daemon log.

**Acceptance criteria**

- With integration enabled and a GitHub `origin`, the TUI new-task form offers an issue picker; selecting an issue fills title, description, link line and matching declared fields, and every one of them is still editable.
- With integration disabled, or on a project whose `origin` is not GitHub, no issue row appears and no GitHub call is made.
- A task created from issue N renders `.Issue.Number`, `.Issue.Title`, `.Issue.Body`, `.Issue.URL` and `.Issue.Labels` in an agent or command step; a task created without one renders the zero value and a `{{ if .Issue.Number }}` template works on both.
- `vincent task create --github-issue N` produces the same stored task as the TUI path; explicit flags override the issue-derived values.
- `vincent github issues` lists selectable issues for a project.
- Editing the issue on GitHub after creation does not change what a later step renders.
- With `gh` absent and no token set: no issue row, a logged reason, and a `vincent doctor` row saying so — task creation without an issue is unaffected.
- Cross-platform: the `gh` invocation and the token fallback both work on Windows, macOS and Linux.

### Alternatives considered

- **Store the GitHub repo on `Project`** (`github_repo: owner/name`, auto-filled at registration, editable). Handles SSH aliases and non-`origin` GitHub remotes, and would let the projects view show the link — but it costs a migration and a new editable field for a fact that is derivable today. Worth revisiting if remote parsing proves too narrow, or when PR checking lands and needs a durable repo identity.
- **Flatten issue data into `Task.Fields`** as `github_issue_number`, `github_issue_body`, … instead of a `.Issue` struct. No new context type and it works in every existing template, but it collides with user-declared field names and flattens labels into a joined string.
- **Store a GitHub token in `config.yaml`.** Self-contained and independent of `gh`, but it makes vincent a secret store, which spec §2 declines.
- **Re-fetch the issue on every step render.** Always current, at the cost of a network call and a new failure mode inside rendering, which today cannot fail for external reasons.
- **Prefill the title only** and leave the body reachable solely through `.Issue.Body`. Keeps the description for the human's own framing, but loses the at-a-glance context on the board and in the detail view.

### Spec reference

§5.1 (Project), §5.3 (Task), §8.1.2 (declared task fields), §8.4 (template context), §13.2 (endpoints), §15 (TUI new-task form). §2 non-goal "secret management (daemon inherits the user's environment)" is what selects the `gh`/env-token approach. Decision record row 11 — "Delivery owned entirely by workflow steps; no hardcoded push/PR/merge behavior" — is not contradicted by this: reading an issue to prefill a task is input, not delivery, and no push, PR or merge behavior is added. That row does become live when PR checking arrives, so the design should keep GitHub access out of the delivery path.
title: GitHub integration: select a GitHub issue when creating a task

body:
### Problem

A step cannot say anything about itself in its own words. Today a reader has two
channels and neither answers "what is this doing" or "why did that fail":

- `failure_reason` is a **closed enum** of daemon-authored constants
  (`timeout`, `nonzero_exit`, `check_failed`, `merge_conflict`, …
  `internal/taskrun/engine.go:23`, `internal/worktree/worktree.go:22`). It says
  which *category* of thing went wrong, never which file, which test, which
  assertion. `nonzero_exit` on a 40-minute agent step is almost no information.
- `step_runs.result_summary` holds the agent's final result text or the last 200
  lines of command stdout. It is stored, exposed on the API DTO
  (`internal/api/tasks.go:234`), and read by `.Steps.<id>.Result` and the repair
  prompt — but it is **never rendered anywhere in the TUI**. The attempt line in
  `internal/tui/detailrender.go:539` shows state, duration, tokens, cost,
  `failure_reason`, `skip_reason` and the agent triple, and nothing else.

So a task that is running tells you only that it is running, and a task that is
blocked tells you only the category of its failure. Finding out more means
opening the transcript, which is the durable output copy — not a summary.

The gap is worst for the two cases in this issue's title:

1. **Live.** A `running` agent step is opaque for its whole duration. On the
   board, a row that has been running for 25 minutes looks identical whether the
   agent is scaffolding a migration or stuck retrying the same failing test.
2. **Terminal.** When a step fails, the step itself usually *knows* why in terms
   a human wants — "3 tests red in internal/store", "no upstream branch" — and
   has no way to say so. The enum flattens all of that to `check_failed`.

### Proposed solution

Let the **running step process emit its own status message**, and carry that
message through the daemon to every client.

**Producing it — a sentinel line in the step's output.** The agent or command
writes a marked line (spelling TBD, e.g. `::vincent:status:: <text>`) to its
output; the daemon recognises it in the stream it already reads and lifts it out
as the step run's current status. This was chosen over a workflow-authored
`status:` template field precisely because the interesting messages are the ones
only the step can know at run time — which test failed, which file conflicted.
A template rendered from the §8.4 context could not produce those.

Open sub-questions for the implementer:

- Where the parse hooks in. Agent steps arrive as a normalized `AgentEvent`
  stream (§9, `Output` events); command steps as raw stdout/stderr. Both funnel
  through `Runner.publishOutput` (`internal/taskrun/runner.go:302`), which is the
  natural single seam.
- Whether a matched sentinel line is **stripped from the transcript and from
  `result_summary`**, or left in place. Stripping keeps `.Steps.<id>.Result` and
  the `<previous-attempt-failure>` retry block clean; leaving it keeps the
  transcript a faithful copy of what the process printed. Prefer leaving the
  transcript untouched and stripping only from the derived summary, but this
  needs deciding, not defaulting.
- Bounds: max length, single-line only, and what happens to a step that emits
  the sentinel in a tight loop. Live output chunks are already droppable for
  slow subscribers (§13.3), but a status is *state* and needs a cap and a
  sane update rate.
- Whether an agent has to be told about the protocol in its prompt for this to
  ever fire in practice, and if so whether the daemon appends that instruction
  automatically the way it appends the retry-failure block (§8.4).

**Lifecycle — both live and terminal.** A running step may update its status any
number of times. The last value set before the attempt ends is retained on the
finished step run as its terminal message, which is what makes "why it failed"
work. So this is one field with two readings, not two features.

**Persistence and API.** A new nullable column on `step_runs` (append-only
migration, `internal/store/migrations/0014_*.sql`), a new field on the step-run
DTO in `internal/api/tasks.go` and `internal/apiclient/tasks.go`, and an SSE
signal when it changes so clients update without polling. Note the §13.3 split:
durable state events are replayable via `Last-Event-ID`, live output chunks are
dropped for slow subscribers. A status update needs to land on the **durable**
side, or a client that blinks loses the message with no way to recover it.

**Surfaces — all four are in scope:**

- TUI detail, on the attempt line beside `failure_reason`
  (`internal/tui/detailrender.go` `attemptLine`).
- TUI board, on the task row, so a running or blocked task explains itself
  without being opened. Board rows are width-constrained; this needs a
  truncation rule, not just an extra field.
- REST + SSE, so curl and scripts see it too.
- The `vincent` CLI task-inspection output.

**Step-type scope — and one thing that does not resolve.** The intent is that
*every* step type can carry a status: `agent`, `command`, `manual`, and the
structure steps (`parallel`, `fan_out`, `condition`, `loop`, `break`).
`include` is out by construction — it is spliced away at task creation (§7.9)
and never reaches the engine.

But a sentinel line requires a process to print it, and only `agent` and
`command` steps have one. `manual` waits on a human; the structure steps
evaluate templates or coordinate children. Those types record `step_run` rows
(`internal/taskrun/engine.go:742` writes the row generically from
`env.step.Type`, and `internal/taskrun/condition.go:66` does the same for
conditions) but they never run a subprocess, so the emit mechanism cannot reach
them as specified. Three ways out, and this needs a maintainer decision before
implementation:

1. Ship the sentinel for `agent` and `command` only, and leave the other types
   with an empty status — smallest change, but "all step types" is not met.
2. Add a workflow-authored `status:` template as the mechanism for the types
   with no process, so `manual` and the structure steps get their status from
   YAML while `agent`/`command` get theirs from the sentinel. Two mechanisms
   feeding one field.
3. Have the daemon synthesise a status for the process-less types from what it
   already knows (a condition's rendered guard and verdict, a loop's iteration
   and item, a group's finished/total lane count). No new authoring surface, but
   it is daemon-authored text, which is what `failure_reason` already is.

### Alternatives considered

- **A workflow-authored `status:` template field on `Step`** rendered against the
  §8.4 context. Rejected as the primary mechanism: it can only restate what the
  workflow author already knew when they wrote the YAML, so it cannot say which
  test failed or which file conflicted. Still on the table as the *secondary*
  mechanism for process-less step types (option 2 above).
- **Just render the existing `result_summary` in the TUI.** Much cheaper — no
  migration, no protocol, no new API field — and it would improve the blocked
  case immediately. Rejected as sufficient because it gives nothing while a step
  is running, and its content is whatever the process happened to print last
  rather than something the step chose to say.
- **Widening the `failure_reason` enum.** Doesn't help: the value is that the
  message is free-form and run-specific. Adding constants keeps it categorical,
  and the enum is deliberately shared vocabulary between `internal/worktree` and
  `internal/taskrun/engine.go` — a `block_reason` means the same thing wherever
  it originated, and free text would break that.
- **Telling people to read the transcript.** This is the status quo. The
  transcript is the durable output copy, not a summary; scanning it is exactly
  the work this issue asks the step to do once, for itself.

### Spec reference

New material, so it amends rather than cites:

- **§5.4 StepRun** — the field list is normative and would gain the status
  message. Note it does not currently list `result_summary` either, which is
  worth fixing in the same pass.
- **§7.2 Failure and retry** — the relationship between a free-text status and
  the `failure_reason` enum, and whether the status reaches the
  `<previous-attempt-failure>` block on retries.
- **§8.4 Template context** — only if a workflow-authored `status:` template is
  adopted for the process-less types, and if `.Steps.<id>` gains the status
  alongside `Status`/`Result`/`ExitCode`.
- **§13.3 Events** — the durable-vs-droppable split; a status update must be
  durable.
- **§15 TUI** — board row and detail attempt line.
- **§9** — whether the sentinel is parsed per-adapter or once over the
  normalized `AgentEvent` stream. Adapters differ in what they can do and those
  differences are documented, never faked, so if any adapter cannot carry the
  sentinel that has to be stated rather than emulated.

Nothing in `docs/tasks/` covers this yet; it would be task 033.
title: Let a step report a custom status message, live and on failure

body:
## Context

AUR support was intentionally removed from `feat/package-distribution-channels` because new AUR account registration is temporarily suspended. The current distribution work should ship without depending on an external onboarding path that cannot be completed or validated.

This issue tracks adding AUR as a separate follow-up once registration is available again.

## Proposed package

- Package name: `vincent-agent-bin`
- `vincent-bin` cannot be used because it belongs to an unrelated terminal color-scheme project.
- Consume vincent's prebuilt GitHub Release archives rather than rebuilding from source.
- Support x86-64 and ARM64.
- Install `/usr/bin/vincent`, `LICENSE`, `COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md`, and `README.md`.
- Declare `git` as a runtime dependency.
- Preserve `PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0` in package metadata.
- Publish stable releases only.

## Work

- [ ] Confirm that AUR account registration and package creation are available again.
- [ ] Create/verify the maintainer AUR account.
- [ ] Generate a dedicated unencrypted Ed25519 key for non-interactive publishing.
- [ ] Register the public key with the AUR account and store the private key as the `AUR_KEY` repository secret.
- [ ] Document that an AUR SSH key authenticates the account and is not server-side scoped to one package.
- [ ] Add the GoReleaser `aurs` configuration for `vincent-agent-bin`.
- [ ] Add snapshot validation for generated `PKGBUILD` and `.SRCINFO` metadata.
- [ ] Restore AUR installation and release-runbook documentation.
- [ ] Bootstrap the package using the latest stable vincent release available at implementation time.
- [ ] Verify installation and upgrade on a clean Arch Linux system with `makepkg -si` (and an AUR helper as a user-facing smoke test).

## Acceptance criteria

- A stable release publishes a valid `PKGBUILD` and `.SRCINFO` to `ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/vincent-agent-bin.git`.
- The package downloads the matching signed/checksummed vincent release archive.
- Both supported architectures install a working `vincent` binary.
- Prereleases and snapshot builds do not update the AUR package.
- Release documentation covers credential setup, rotation, publication verification, installation, upgrade, and removal.
title: Add AUR distribution when registration reopens

body:
Parent review: #135
Reviewed baseline: [7b621865](https://github.com/lezli01/vincent/commit/7b6218658b040d03aeece9dc4bba78a5369d6a2b)
Priority: **P2 — integration reliability**
Area: Claude, Codex, Cursor adapters

## Problem

Vincent depends on third-party CLI flags, permission semantics, model options, stream schemas, and authentication behavior that can change independently. Version/help probing exists, but there is no explicit compatibility contract that tells a user whether the installed CLI version was tested, merely detected, or is known incompatible.

A vendor update can therefore turn a previously deterministic run into startup failure, malformed stream handling, changed permission behavior, or silent loss of metrics.

## Proposed direction

- For each adapter, maintain a tested minimum/maximum or capability-probed compatibility matrix by vincent release.
- Prefer capability probes over brittle version ranges where help/schema behavior can be tested safely.
- Separate installed, authenticated, protocol-compatible, permission-compatible, and model-catalog health.
- Cache probe results with binary identity/mtime/version and invalidate on binary/config changes.
- Surface compatibility in doctor, GET /agents, TUI workflow selection, task plan, and debug transcripts.
- Fail closed for incompatible security-relevant behavior; allow explicit warnings only for non-security unknown versions.
- Add fixtures for old/current/future/unknown stream fields and help output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each adapter documents tested CLI versions and required capabilities.
- [ ] doctor distinguishes missing, unauthenticated, unsupported platform, incompatible protocol, incompatible permission mode, and unknown-but-allowed version.
- [ ] Security-sensitive missing capabilities fail before task creation/admission.
- [ ] Unknown JSON fields remain forward compatible where safe; malformed/oversized frames fail explicitly.
- [ ] Binary updates invalidate cached probe/catalog results.
- [ ] CI tests adapter probes against versioned fake fixtures, including removed/renamed flags.
- [ ] Release notes state adapter compatibility changes.
title: [P2][agents] Define adapter version compatibility and protocol health checks

body:
Parent review: #135
Reviewed baseline: [7b621865](https://github.com/lezli01/vincent/commit/7b6218658b040d03aeece9dc4bba78a5369d6a2b)
Priority: **P2 — secure-development defense in depth**
Area: CI, lint, static analysis

## Problem

The normal golangci configuration enables a strong quality set but not gosec. The source already contains targeted nolint:gosec annotations, suggesting security-linter use was anticipated.

Evidence: [.golangci.yml](https://github.com/lezli01/vincent/blob/7b6218658b040d03aeece9dc4bba78a5369d6a2b/.golangci.yml#L1-L22)

A standalone review run produced 42 raw findings. These were not 42 vulnerabilities: most were expected reports around intentional process execution, fixed SQL construction, test fake agents, and impractical integer conversions. Two useful signals—workflow file loading and config modes—were promoted into dedicated P0/P1 issues.

## Proposed direction

- Enable gosec in the pinned normal toolchain or add a pinned separate target.
- Baseline every current finding with a narrow code-local suppression and reason; avoid a blanket rule disable where a small wrapper/helper can prove safety.
- Treat newly introduced unsuppressed findings as CI failures.
- Keep manual review for exec, path, SQL, permission, and integer reports; scanner output is evidence, not a verdict.
- Consider CodeQL, secret scanning, and SBOM generation as separate defense-in-depth tasks, not substitutes for gosec or govulncheck.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pinned gosec version runs locally and in CI.
- [ ] Current findings are fixed or individually suppressed with accurate rationale.
- [ ] No suppression uses a misleading daemon-owned/trusted-path assertion where repository input reaches the path.
- [ ] New unsuppressed findings fail CI.
- [ ] Generated/test/fakeagent scope is explicitly configured.
- [ ] Contributor/security docs explain gosec versus govulncheck.
- [ ] CI runtime remains bounded and the exact local command matches CI.
title: [P2][security] Add gosec to the normal static-analysis gate with reviewed suppressions
